overview: Namibia has almost no dedicated femtech startup sector, so its women's health innovation runs mostly through government policy and UN/NGO reproductive-health programs. Momentum in 2025 was driven from the top: Dr Esperance Luvindao, appointed at 34 as Africa's youngest health minister and herself the founder of a women's-health foundation, launched a Universal Health Coverage Policy and a new Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Adolescent Health and Nutrition strategy, alongside a national HPV vaccination rollout. A nascent but real startup ecosystem is forming around the Basecamp incubator and the new USD 10M Ndjaba Seed Fund, which includes healthtech in its scope though not a specific gender lens.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: The biggest 2025 developments were policy launches and vaccination drives led by a reform-minded health ministry.

items.text: Dr Esperance Luvindao, 34, founder of the Osaat Africa Health Foundation, sworn in as Minister of Health and Social Services, becoming Africa's youngest health minister.
National HPV vaccination campaign launched targeting 232,000 girls aged 9-14 across all 14 regions; about 65,000 vaccinated in the first two weeks.
Ministry of Health launches the Universal Health Coverage Policy and 2025/26-2029/30 Strategic Plan in Windhoek.
New York Times profiles Minister Luvindao and her efforts to reimagine Namibian health care.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Namibia has moved on both reproductive-health strategy and menstrual-product affordability.

items.text: VAT Amendment Act reclassifies sanitary pads as zero-rated, removing the 15% tax to ease period poverty (championed by Deputy Minister Emma Theofelus).
National Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Adolescent Health and Nutrition Strategy 2025/26-2029/30 launched in Windhoek with WHO support.
Universal Health Coverage Policy launched to guarantee essential services without financial hardship.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: The broader startup ecosystem is early-stage; health-specific femtech activity is thin and mostly foundation-led.

items.text: Osaat Africa Health Foundation (founded 2019) runs Menga, a digital platform for medication access in informal settlements, and published Emily's Health, a women's-health book in eight local languages.
BOOSTUP 2025/26 early-stage support programme launched with NCRST, NIPDB and Basecamp; 20 startups selected from 30 applicants.
UNFPA supports mobile clinics extending sexual and reproductive health services to adolescents and youth in underserved areas.
Start-Up Namibia (GIZ-supported) works to strengthen the country's overall startup ecosystem.

sections.heading: Notable funding rounds
sections.narrative: There are no disclosed femtech-specific rounds; the relevant capital is a new generalist seed fund with healthtech scope and program grants.

items.purpose: Backing 35-50 early-stage Southern African startups incl. healthtech; tickets USD 25K-350K over a 10-year horizon.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
sections.narrative: The ecosystem is anchored by the health ministry, UN agencies, one women's-health foundation and a small set of incubators/funds.

items.name: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS)
items.note: Leads UHC, RMNCAH, HPV and family-planning programs under Minister Esperance Luvindao.

items.name: Osaat Africa Health Foundation
items.note: Women's-health education, contraceptive access and digital health (Menga platform); founded by the current health minister.

items.name: UNFPA Namibia
items.note: Comprehensive sexuality education, contraceptive access, mobile SRH clinics and menstrual-health awareness.

items.name: WHO Namibia
items.note: Technical partner on maternal health, HPV/cervical cancer and UHC frameworks.

items.name: Project HOPE Namibia
items.note: Lead implementer of the PEPFAR-funded DREAMS HIV-prevention program for adolescent girls and young women.

items.name: Basecamp Business Incubator
items.note: Windhoek incubator (est. 2023) running BOOSTUP and supplying pipeline for the Ndjaba Seed Fund.

items.name: Namibia Investment Promotion and Development Board (NIPDB)
items.note: Co-runs the BOOSTUP early-stage startup support programme.

sections.heading: Active investors
sections.narrative: Capital for women's health is program-based (UN/PEPFAR) plus one local generalist fund; gender-lens VCs active in Southern Africa are regional rather than Namibia-specific.

items.name: Bellatrix Investment Managers (Ndjaba Seed Fund)
items.role: USD 10M seed fund covering healthtech among target sectors for Southern African startups.

items.name: PEPFAR / USAID
items.role: Funds the DREAMS HIV-prevention program for adolescent girls and young women.

items.name: UNFPA
items.role: Funds and supports adolescent SRH, family planning and menstrual-health work in Namibia.

items.name: Afrishela
items.role: Gender-lens fund providing impact-linked loans to women-owned businesses across East and Southern Africa.

items.name: UNICEF Femtech Ventures
items.role: Five-year (2025-2030) platform funding women's-health startups; over half of applicants from Africa.
